text.p: Israel's Shin Bet security service has banned the Jerusalem bureau chief of the London-based Al-Hayat newspaper from entering the disputed city, an Israeli official said.

Ruba Husari, 33, has covered Israel, the West Bank and the Gaza Strip for the Arabic newspaper since 1989, entering Israel and Arab East Jerusalem from her home in Ramallah with a permit issued by the Jewish state's occupation authority known as the civil administration.
Civil administration spokesman Peter Lerner said on Tuesday the Shin Bet ordered the administration last December to stop renewing the permit.
"They (the Shin Bet) cited security reasons," Lerner told Reuters, saying the security service did not elaborate.
Husari described the claim as "baseless" and said she was baffled by the decision.
"How can I be the Jerusalem bureau chief for Al-Hayat without being able to enter Israel? It's nonsense," she told Reuters.
Al-Hayat is one of the world's most widely distributed Arabic-language newspapers.
